title: Introduce policy sandbox and prioritized regional routing queue to reduce hotpath contention
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: The current policy evaluation and fallback decision path executes synchronously on the routing hotpath. Under bursty traffic patterns this creates lock contention and CPU stalls which increase p95/p99 latencies and exacerbate fallback storms during regional capacity pressure. Several prior tickets modularized pieces of the pipeline, but we still observe contention around policy lookups, validation, and fallback admission logic.

Goal: Reduce routing hotpath contention and enable safer rollouts for policy changes by: 1) introducing a lightweight "policy sandbox" that validates and scores policy changes off-hotpath, and 2) adding a prioritized, non-blocking regional routing queue that separates fast-path satisfied requests from heavyweight policy-evaluated requests. This should reduce tail latency, make fallbacks less noisy, and allow staged policy activation with metric-driven promotion.

Non-goals: Full rewrite of the router. Not touching long-lived regional leases/API surface for affinities in this ticket. Not implementing a full policy language runtime (we will validate with existing protobuf policy objects).

Design overview and trade-offs: 
- Policy sandbox: a small, sidecar-like worker pool (configurable size) that accepts policy change bundles and synthetic or sampled real requests to validate semantics (compatibility, request classification, estimated cost, fallback risk). Sandbox runs off the hotpath and emits a "confidence score" and divergence trace. Trade-offs: additional infra and slight config complexity, but avoids blocking the main router for validation.
- Prioritized routing queue: introduce a two-tier in-memory queue per region: fast-path queue (no policy or cached acceptance) and slow-path queue (requires sandbox validation or miss). Request admission uses optimistic reads of cached policy decisions and KV cache; on miss, request is enqueued on slow-path and a best-effort async evaluation happens. We enforce soft quotas and backpressure: when slow-path queue exceeds threshold we apply graceful demotion to compatible model variants or regional spillover rather than blocking callers.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Prototype sandbox worker and scoring API (local dev + unit tests). Add instrumentation events: sandbox.enter, sandbox.exit, sandbox.score, sandbox.diverged.
2) Add prioritized queue data structure behind a feature flag. Implement optimistic fast-path check and enqueue-on-miss semantics.
3) Integrate sandbox scoring into slow-path processing and store short-lived decision leases in a bounded LRU cache.
4) Add graceful demotion policy and regional spillover policy adapters.
5) End-to-end test harness with synthetic burst scenarios and replay of historical traces from observability.
6) Gradual rollout: start with 5% of requests in a non-critical region, monitor latencies/fallbacks, then 25%/50%/100%.

Observability and release criteria:
- Instrumentation: new metrics (sandbox_latency_ms, sandbox_confidence, slowpath_enqueue_rate, slowpath_demotion_rate, fastpath_hit_rate), and traces tagged with routing.sa-sandbox and routing.queue-tier.
- SLO guardrails: p50/p95/p99 latency should not regress for overall requests in controlled rollout; slow-path p95 may temporarily rise but system-level p99 should decrease.
- Telemetry checks: divergence rate between sandbox decisions and current live decisions must be < 0.5% before promotion.

Backward compatibility and data model changes:
- No external API changes. Internal policy protobuf remains compatible; sandbox uses same protobuf but accepts a "validation bundle" wrapper.
- Decision lease cache TTL default 1s (configurable).

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests: sandbox scoring logic, prioritized queue ordering, backpressure demotion behavior.
- Integration tests: simulate mixed workload with varying sequence lengths and KV cache hit ratios.
- Load tests: reproduce previous production contention scenarios and validate p99 improvements.
- Chaos tests: kill sandbox worker pool and verify router falls back to baseline behavior with no request loss.

Migration and rollback plan:
- Feature-flagged rollout.
- Fast rollback toggles to disable prioritized queue and sandbox; when toggled off, system returns to prior synchronous evaluation path.
- Canary run on staging region for 48 hours with synthetic spike injection before production canary.

Open questions and risks:
- How to measure "confidence" consistently across model variants and region-specific overrides? (We will normalize scores by request complexity and sequence length.)
- Resource isolation: sandbox workers must not contend with serving runtime GPU/CPU. Plan: force sandbox onto control-plane class machines or set cpu shares.
- Observability cost: added events could increase telemetry volume; we will sample traces and aggregate metrics at 1s resolution.

Artifacts and links: 
- Design doc: https://confluence.internal.redwood/projects/ROUTING/pages/Policy+Sandbox+Design (placeholder)
- Benchmark infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1234 (placeholder)
- Draft prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/compare/feature/sandbox-queue (placeholder)

Acceptance criteria (pre-merge):
- Unit and integration test suite coverage for new queue and sandbox > 90% of new code.
- Benchmarks showing p99 routing latency improvement by at least 10% under synthetic bursts compared to baseline.
- Telemetry pipeline emits the new metrics and can compute divergence within 5 minutes of ingestion.

Post-merge rollout steps:
- Deploy to canary region with feature flag OFF by default and sandbox in dry-run mode capturing predictions for 24h.
- Turn on prioritized queue for 5% of traffic with sandbox scoring active. Monitor metrics for 72h.
- Promote traffic share if metrics are stable and divergence < 0.5%.

Estimated effort and owners:
- Core routing engineer (assignee): 8 points (Ravi Patel)
- Observability engineer: 2 points (review + dashboards)
- SRE: 2 points (deploy hooks, runtime config)

Expected follow-ups:
- Policy language incremental optimizer (separate ticket).
- Storage-backed longer-lived decision cache for cold-start scenarios (separate ticket).
